in_hebrew.name: ברתולומיאוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ברתולומיאוס הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'בן תלמי' או 'בן האדמה'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'בן' שפירושו 'בן' או 'ילד', ו'תלמי' שפירושו 'האדמה' או 'השדה'. השם נמצא בברית החדשה ומתייחס לאחד מתלמידי ישו.

in_greek.name: Βαρθολομαῖος
in_greek.long_meaning: Βαρθολομαῖος (Batholomew) σημαίνει 'υἱὸς τοῦ Θαλμαίου' (בן תלמי). Ονομάζεται έτσι από τον Εβραϊκό 'ברתולומיאוס' (Bartholomaios), που προέρχεται από τις λέξεις 'בן' (בן) και 'תלמי' (תלמי). Στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ματθαίου (Ματθαῖος 10:3), ο Βαρθολομαῖος αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους δώδεκα αποστόλους του Ιησού.

in_latin.name: Batholomew
in_latin.meaning: son of Thalmi, son of the earth
in_latin.long_meaning: Batholomew, derived from the Hebrew 'ברתולומיאוס' (Bartholomaios), signifies 'son of Thalmi' or 'son of the earth'. The name Thalmi is believed to be related to the Hebrew word for 'earth' or 'soil'. In the Latin tradition, Bartholomew is known as one of Jesus' twelve apostles, often associated with evangelizing the Gospel to the Gentiles.

in_english.name: Batholomew
in_english.meaning: son of Thalmi, son of the earth, farmer
in_english.long_meaning: The name Batholomew originates from the Hebrew 'ברתולומיאוס' (Bartholomaios), meaning 'son of Thalmi' or 'son of the earth'. Thalmi is thought to derive from the Hebrew word for 'earth', 'soil', or 'farmer'. In Christian tradition, Bartholomew (or Batholomew) is recognized as one of Jesus' twelve apostles. He is often associated with spreading the Gospel to various regions, including Armenia and parts of Asia Minor. The name symbolizes a connection to the land and possibly agricultural roots. Throughout history, the name has been adapted into various languages, maintaining its significant spiritual and cultural heritage.

data.cultural_impact: Batholomew was a beloved and revered apostle in early Christian history, known as Nathanael in the New Testament. He is often depicted in art as a tall, heavy man or as an old, bearded hermit, reflecting his reputation as a strong and wise follower of Christ. The feast day of St. Batholomew is celebrated on August 24th, and he is the patron saint of various places, including prodigals, farmers, and those with physical ailments. His story of conversion is one of the most dramatic in the Bible, and his image has influenced religious art and iconography for centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Batholomew carries the message of dedication to God and the reminder of the power of conversion. For Christians, the life of St. Batholomew serves as an inspiration to live a life fully devoted to God, no matter one's background or past mistakes. His story of being identified as a 'man truly without guile' (John 1:47) by Jesus highlights the importance of honesty and authenticity in one's spiritual journey. Furthermore, the feast day of St. Batholomew offers an opportunity for all Christians to reflect on their own commitment to God and seek His guidance in their lives.
